data.claim: A line-based parser keyed by doc/name, rebuilding only region spans, keeps every other byte (CRLF, no final newline) identical
data.falsifier: any byte outside a region differs after splice
data.mechanism: splice copies old[cur:begin] verbatim between region spans
data.question: Can regions be spliced by name leaving outside text byte-identical?

evidence.note: ran ddflow brief --item B-tpl-regions; decisions D-doc-regions, D-small-files honoured

chunk_findings.detail: The new named-region path is selected by substring-scanning the *rendered body* rather than the template/its declared mode. A REGION-mode template still in the legacy dialect whose generated content happens to contain the literal `ddflow:begin <doc>/` — e.g. a doc whose body documents/exemplifies the marker grammar (marker examples are exactly the kind of text a template that "is skeleton and source" for the marker docs would emit), or any user-authored text quoting an example marker with the same doc kind — will be routed into `RG.write_named`. `write_named` requires every template region to already exist in the target file by name; a legacy target file contains only `DDFLOW:BEGIN` markers, so every region is reported "missing from the file" and the update is refused/fails, where the legacy `W.write_region` path would have written it correctly. So given input "legacy template + existing legacy file + a region body containing `<!-- ddflow:begin export/summary sha=... -->`", line 339 returns `write_named(...)` and the write regresses. The branch decision should be keyed on the template source / an explicit mode flag, not on bytes that legitimately appear in rendered content.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:339 (`if f"ddflow:begin {spec.doc}/" in body`)

chunk_findings.detail: `splice` converts the freshly rendered region (markers and body) to CRLF *after* `render_region(doc, r.name, bodies[r.name])` has already hashed the (LF) body and baked that digest into the `sha=` field of the begin marker — the digest is never recomputed for the converted text. Concretely, take a target file whose region lines use CRLF (e.g. a repo checked out on Windows with `core.autocrlf`, or any file whose begin line carries `\r\n`). `parse` yields the region, `sp.text` is written with an LF-based `sha`, but the bytes stored between the markers are CRLF. On the very next `ddflow ... update` for that doc, `parse` returns the region, `Region.edited` evaluates `F.body_digest(content)` where `content` is now the CRLF body, so `body_digest(content) != sha` and `write_named` raises the refusal "region(s) body of <file> were edited by hand since ddflow wrote them; refusing to overwrite (--force to replace)". Nothing was hand-edited — ddflow's own line-ending conversion changed the bytes — yet every subsequent update on a CRLF file is refused unless `--force` is passed. In other words, the code writes a file that its own `edited` check immediately classifies as hand-modified. The digest must be computed over the string as it will land in the file (or `body_digest`/`Region.edited` must hash a newline-normalized body) so that the recorded `sha` matches the stored CRLF content.

chunk_findings.detail: `render()` gained a `doc` parameter and unconditionally stuffs it into the context as `DOC_KEY`, and `render_kind` was updated to pass `doc=k.name` — but the sibling render path for document kinds, `render_document`, still calls `render()` without a `doc`, so `DOC_KEY` is silently `""` there instead of the kind/document name. Since the region macro is registered as a plain global (`env.globals["region"] = region`) and can only learn the document name from the context, any document-kind template containing `{% call region("body") %}` emits markers with an empty document name. Concretely: a file whose regions were written under the legacy `doc=<kind>` dialect (or written through the kind path, which now uses `k.name`) is re-rendered by `render_document` with `doc == ""`; the update/splice path matches regions by that document name, so the region is not located, the body is never updated, and the legacy markers are never rewritten — contradicting the stated intent ("update renders, extracts each region body and splices it into the file by name", "reads the legacy dialects (doc=, DDFLOW:BEGIN) and rewrites them on the first write"). Because the new parameter defaults to `""`, this mismatch produces no error at all; the failure is silent. The `doc` name needs to be threaded through `render_document` (or the default must be rejected/derived) before region markers can be relied on for document kinds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/registry.py:render_document (render default at line 453, `ctx[DOC_KEY] = doc`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The expected value of the central assertion is derived from the output being tested:

```python
assert sp.text == SKELETON.replace("A1\n", "A2\n").replace(
    RG.parse(SKELETON)[0].sha, RG.parse(sp.text)[0].sha
)
```

`RG.parse(sp.text)[0].sha` reads the hash out of `sp.text`, i.e. the very text on the left. Take `SKELETON` with region `d/a` body `"A1\n"` and marker `sha=S0`. If `splice` replaces the body with `"A2\n"` but never recomputes the marker hash (leaving the stale `S0`), then `sp.text == SKELETON.replace("A1\n","A2\n")` and `RG.parse(sp.text)[0].sha == S0`, so `.replace(S0, S0)` is a no-op and the assertion passes — the hash clause verifies nothing. Nothing else in the file covers this: the only later hash-sensitive check, `RG.write_named(..., check=True)` in `test_write_named_create_update_and_hand_edit`, runs after a `force=True` write whose template body (`A1\n`) hashes to the stale `S0`, so it returns `code == 0` for a "never updates the hash" implementation too. Consequence: a splicer that writes the new body but leaves the stale body hash — which makes the freshly updated region parse as hand-edited (`edited=True`), so the next `write_named`/`check` fails with `ExportError` code 3 and the documented hand-edit detection inverts — passes this entire suite. A direct check would need the expected text built independently, e.g. asserting `RG.parse(sp.text)[0].sha != RG.parse(SKELETON)[0].sha` and `not RG.parse(sp.text)[0].edited` after the body change.
